topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture on Complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture, framing complement as a complex but essential immunological process with challenging nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement Overview, Nomenclature, and the Central Role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental principles of the complement system, outlining its primary functions, historical naming conventions, and the central mechanism of C3 activation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Complement Recognition and Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three upstream pathways—alternative, lectin, and classical—that initiate complement activation and converge on surface C3 convertase formation.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of the Complement Cascade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three primary downstream effector outcomes of complement activation: opsonization for phagocytosis, inflammation induction, and direct pathogen lysis via the membrane attack complex.

topics.label: Host Regulation and Protection from Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that prevent complement from spontaneously activating on and damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Consequences of Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the distinct clinical presentations and disease risks associated with genetic or acquired deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen Evasion Mechanisms and Staphylococcal Adaptations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evolve strategies to evade complement-mediated killing, highlighting the multifaceted evasion tactics of Staphylococcus aureus and their biomedical applications.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Next Steps
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and outlines the upcoming transition to the adaptive immune system.
